label: malicious
signal: SMS read+send combo + critical YARA family match (scoring.py:_check_yara)
note: Banking trojan sideloaded from a WhatsApp forward ('wedding invite', 'KYC update'). What separates it from apk/benign-sms-app is the YARA family match - the two carry byte-identical permission sets, which is why permission volume was removed from scoring. Reaches only Suspicious (55) because one critical YARA match is worth 40; see the finding below.
finding: A YARA rule that NAMES a malware family (Drinik, njRAT, AsyncRAT, FakeCalls) is artifact-identity evidence, as strong as a hash match, but scores the same 40 as a generic behaviour rule. Deliberately NOT fixed by raising APK permission weights - that would recreate the benign-sms-app false positive. The real fix is separating family-naming rules from generic behaviour rules (PDF_AutoAction, Generic_Ransomware_Note), which needs benign YARA cases first because the generic rules are FP-prone.
